text.what: A narrow slate valley south of Bonn, among the smallest German regions and the one that gives more of its ground to spätburgunder than any other.
text.story: Steep terraces on a river that runs east-west, this far north, on dark stone that holds the day's heat. The July 2021 flood tore through the valley and its cellars; growers were still rebuilding years after.

kin.as: Called spätburgunder here, and grown in a higher share than anywhere else in Germany.
The early-ripening cousin the valley kept.
The other German pinot region, warmer and far larger.

text.story.note: the 2021 flood is general knowledge here, not taken from the corpus
